title: SEO vs AEO vs GEO
text:
SEO, AEO and GEO are NOT the same thing.

Understanding the difference is crucial in 2026:

Your next customer isn't only searching Google anymore.

They're asking ChatGPT "who's the best in town?"
They're reading Google's AI answer and never scrolling down.

That competitor who's always booked out? They already show up in all three places.

You don't need a marketing department to do the same.
You just need to know what each one is:

SEO (Search Engine Optimisation)

What it is: Getting your website to show up when locals search Google.

How it works:
- Give each service people search for its own page.
- Get trusted sites to link to you.

✅ Pros: A steady stream of calls and bookings.
❌ Cons: Takes a few months to kick in.

How to rank higher:
- Build pages around what you sell and where.
- Fix site problems and refresh pages every few months.

AEO (Answer Engine Optimisation)

What it is: Getting your answers shown in Google's AI box at the top.

How it works:
- Answer the questions customers ask you every day, short and direct.
- Tag those answers so Google can read them.

✅ Pros: You look like the expert before anyone visits your site.
❌ Cons: Some people get the answer and never click.

How to rank higher:
- Answer each question in 40 to 60 words under a clear heading.
- Put your common questions on one FAQ page.

GEO (Generative Engine Optimisation)

What it is: Getting ChatGPT to name YOUR business when someone asks for a recommendation.

How it works:
- Publish clear pages about what you do, with real facts.
- Be where AI looks: reviews, local directories, articles.

✅ Pros: Most of your competitors aren't doing it yet.
❌ Cons: Hard to track what it brings in.

How to rank higher:
- Say plainly who you serve, where, and why you're different.
- Keep collecting reviews and mentions.

That's three different jobs.
And you already have one: running your business.

Now picture this.

You tell ChatGPT: "Get my business found on Google, in the AI answers and in ChatGPT."

It could do it. It's only missing the data: what people in your city search, where you rank, and who AI recommends instead of you.

title: Ghosted: rank #1, lose the click
text:
Ghosted

👻

SEO in 2026 is just like dating.

You can do everything right and still get stood up.

You rank on page one. Your page is good. And the customer never shows up, because Google's AI answered the question before they got to you.

In early 2026, 68% of US Google searches ended without a click on anything.

AKA...

Ranking is no longer the finish line.
Getting picked is.

Pew Research tracked 68,879 real Google searches. With an AI summary on top, people clicked a regular result on 8% of visits. Without one, on 15%. Only 1% clicked a link inside the summary.

Yeesh.

So, who still gets the customer?

Here's what the data shows:

1) The map still owns "near me".
On plain "near me" searches, Google showed the map with 3 local businesses 93% of the time, and an AI Overview only about 15% of the time.
Keep your Google Business Profile complete: hours, photos, services, reviews. That's where the calls come from.

2) Questions go to the AI.
60% of searches that start with who, what, when or why got an AI summary. Only 8% of one or two word searches did.
Answer those questions on your own site, short answer first, so the AI has something to quote.

3) Your name still gets clicks.
People who already know you search for you by name. Reviews, local news and "best of" lists are how they learn it.

But how do you know which of your searches show a map, which show plain links, and which show an AI answer?

You could check them one by one.

title: What one Google Ads click costs
text:
"What does one Google Ads click cost a local business?" We pulled 18 of the most common "near me" searches in Ubersuggest to find out. Here's what one click costs in the US:

- Personal injury lawyer: $151.27
- Emergency plumber: $72.72
- AC repair: $45.18
- Plumber: $38.80
- Dentist: $13.35

That's per click. Not per customer.

Here's what we think:

A click you pay for is rented. Stop paying, and it's gone the next morning.
A click from ranking on Google costs nothing per click, and it keeps coming.

"Emergency plumber near me" gets 90,500 searches a month in the US. Every click on the ad for it costs $72.72. Every click on the regular results costs $0.

And the price doesn't follow how popular a search is.
"Dentist near me" gets 1.83 million searches a month, at $13.35 a click.
"Personal injury lawyer near me" gets 301,000, at 11x the price.

The more a click costs in your business, the more a ranking is worth.

The AI built on Google Search and Google Maps.

The fastest-rising AI.

Where it looks: Brave Search, plus its own crawler. Its leaked instructions tell it to favor original sources over directories.
Who it names: businesses with detailed pages of their own.
⚠️ Watch out: it skips low-quality sources like forums.

title: Plot twist: AI gets your business wrong
text:
Plot twist

😬

Asking ChatGPT about your own business is like reading your own reviews.

You should do it. You won't like all of it.

When 1,704 companies checked what AI said about them, they flagged 9.2% of the facts as false.
Small companies got it worse: 9.4% false, against 6.3% for large ones.
The most common mistake? Prices. 13.5% of them were wrong.

And in one test of 7 AI tools, 36% of the phone numbers they gave for companies were wrong.

AKA...

A customer can ask ChatGPT for your number, get the wrong one, and call someone else.

Yikes.

Here's the good news.
AI doesn't invent your details out of thin air. It copies them from somewhere.
Fix the source, and you fix the answer.

Here's where each one looks:

1) Gemini reads Google Maps.
Your Google Business Profile is what Gemini reads about you. In a study of almost 2 million local AI citations, Google Business Profiles were the #1 source: 28.6% of them.

2) ChatGPT reads Yelp.
On ChatGPT, Yelp was the #1 cited source for local questions. And in July 2026, Yelp confirmed a deal that puts its reviews, ratings and photos inside ChatGPT.

3) Perplexity reads Tripadvisor.
It pays for Tripadvisor's reviews and listings, 11 million+ businesses.

4) Siri reads Apple Business Connect.
Free, and it controls what iPhone users see in Apple Maps and Siri.

What to do this week:
- Ask ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity: "What are the hours, prices and phone number of [your business]?"
- Write down every wrong answer.
- Fix it at the source: Google Business Profile, Yelp, Tripadvisor, Apple Business Connect.
- Put your prices on your own website. That's what AI gets wrong most.

Then keep checking. The answers change every week.

title: Clicks under AI Overviews, month by month

text:

Here's what we think:

Customers want the price first. Almost nobody gives it to them.
That's the easiest gap in local SEO.

"Call for a quote" doesn't answer the search.
So the customer keeps searching, and books with whoever does answer.

It matters even more in AI search.
Google's AI Overviews and ChatGPT can only quote a price that's written somewhere. If it isn't on your site, the AI quotes someone else's.

You don't need one exact number. A range works:
"Single implant with crown from $X to $Y. Here's what changes the price."
"Roof replacement from $X to $Y per square foot. Here's what changes it."
